registry_info.name: slack_yard
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `slack` family (12 registry names, 3 scripts, 1 shared const). One span stood up five times so the four drawing conventions can be measured against the one that is the solution.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The `slack` word and its five values are PRELOADED from big_pipe_system.gd at runtime and validated at _ready; do not retype them here or in the script.

slack_yard.name: Slack Yard
slack_yard.description: One span, stood up five times. Two masts carry 3.30 m of line across a 3.00 m gap in five parallel lanes, and each lane draws that same line by a different convention: chord, spline, catenary, festoon, truss — the family's five words, read out of big_pipe_system's own const at build time and lettered on a tab at the head of each kerb. One of the five is the actual solution; the yard exists so the other four can be measured against it. `rig` changes the hanging problem (level, a bight, a two-step rise, a raked span) and `datum` changes how much of the measurement is present (none; the true curve repeated in every lane; offset sticks at thirteen stations; a mean column and a peak collar at the head of each lane). Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random: one catenary solve per span at build time, read five ways.
interactions: walk the rank and find the lane with no sticks in it
compare the near truss against the far chord — they measure the same
at scored, read the column against the collar and notice they rank the five differently
switch rig to stepped and watch the batten drop 0.85 m below the middle mast
slack_yard.qfep_connection: Five drawings of one situation, only one of which is the answer, and no stable runner-up: which convention is nearly right depends on the rig, so the ranking is a property of the encounter and not of the conventions. The `scored` rung is the artifact's own dark spot — the moment the yard stops showing a measurement and starts showing a number — and it is built so the two summaries of the same thirteen numbers visibly disagree.
slack_yard.relationships: Synthesised from the twelve registry names that declare `slack`, which resolve to three scripts and one shared const. Replaces none of them and re-runs none of their axes from the outside.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The apron is 2.30 m across the lanes by 3.30 m along the span, so a 3 x 4 clear patch. The lane name tabs stand on the +Z edge and the score gauge at the +Z end of each lane, so the artifact reads correctly approached from +Z; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. There is no collider anywhere in the file, so the pathfinder will route straight through the masts — correct, because there are no masts, there is a picture of a yard.

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the geometry; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every drawn node in this artifact is a MeshInstance3D. X is the apron width 2.30 (five lanes at 0.50 pitch = 2.00, plus 0.15 m of margin each side). Z is the apron length 3.30, which is also the length of the line. Y runs from 0 (the apron underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 2.25 = the `raked` rig's high mast at 2.20 plus half its 0.10 crosshead. The other three rigs top out at 1.85; the union is the box framing was derived from.

dna.axis_shape: `rig` sits SIDE BY SIDE — four different classical hanging problems, none of which contains another, so they are a set and any two of them are a comparison. `datum` NESTS — none is contained in beside is contained in gauged is contained in scored, each rung keeping every mark the last one drew, so it is a sequence and must be swept in order. Both cases are named because they call for opposite handling under trimming: dropping the tail of a parallel axis loses a case, dropping the tail of a nested one only lowers the ceiling.
dna.default:
rig=level, datum=gauged. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is
nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in
doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That
freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `level` AND NOT `bight`. `bight` is the loudest rig — 2.2 slack, a 1.3605 m sag, every
convention obviously wrong — and it is exactly the wrong default, because a frame in which the
answer is obvious is a frame that does not need the yard. `level` is the case all twelve family
members effectively ship, and it is the case where all five conventions are DEFENSIBLE: a true sag
of 0.6009 against a drawn 0.45, five plausible pictures. A visitor who meets only the default meets
the question. `stepped` and `raked` are the rigs that answer it, and they are one token away.

WHY `gauged` AND NOT `none`. `none` is the emptiest rung by definition: five curves and no way to
say which is right, which is a picture of the problem and not of the artifact. `gauged` is the
first rung where the yard's own claim is legible without reading a label — the catenary lane is
the only one of the five with no orange sticks growing out of it, and that absence is the whole
argument, visible in a still, at a glance, without a caption. `scored` was considered and passed
over: it is the strongest single frame but it hands the visitor a number before they have seen the
measurement it came from, and the rung exists precisely to show that the number depends on which
summary you take.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the twelve `slack` declarations leave unbuilt: every member's own note describes the five conventions as a comparison, and not one of them can stand two of them at once.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A YARD RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

A hanging line between two points is ONE physical situation with five drawing conventions laid
over it: the interpolating spline that ignores gravity, the straight chord that denies the hang
entirely, the catenary that is the actual solution, the festoon that repeats the solution
decoratively, and the truss that replaces hanging with structure. Twelve registry names declare
this word, and every one of them STANDS IN one convention and forgoes the other four. None of
them can put the four next to the one that is true, because a body can only be shaped one way at
a time.

So the yard stands the same span five times, in five lanes, on one apron, and varies the PROBLEM
instead of the drawing. The five lanes are identical in colour, radius and emitter, so nothing
distinguishes them except the shape each convention produces from the same 3.30 m of line between
the same two anchors.

WHAT IT FOUND, all solved in Python before anything was built (13 stations, metres,
mean / peak departure from the true curve):

  rig      chord          spline         catenary       festoon        truss
  level    0.4057/0.6009  0.1050/0.1509  0.0001/0.0001  0.3055/0.6009  0.4057/0.6009
  bight    0.9800/1.3605  0.6793/0.9105  0.0003/0.0007  0.7389/1.3605  0.9800/1.3605
  stepped  0.1673/0.2506  0.3346/0.8500  0.0001/0.0002  0.1260/0.2192  0.1673/0.2506
  raked    0.3380/0.5022  0.0373/0.0558  0.0001/0.0001  0.2546/0.5022  0.3380/0.5022

THREE THINGS IN THAT TABLE ARE THE ARTIFACT.

(1) THERE IS NO RUNNER-UP. The ranking INVERTS between rigs. At `level` the draughtsman's batten
is the second-best convention (0.1050) and the chord is the worst (0.4057). At `stepped` the
batten is the WORST (0.3346) and the chord is the best of the four (0.1673), because a batten
drawn end to end across a two-span run passes 0.8500 m below the middle mast it is anchored to,
while a chord at least touches all three anchors. Which convention is nearly right is a property
of the rig, not of the convention. That is why `rig` is the axis and `slack` is the exhibit.

(2) CHORD AND TRUSS MEASURE IDENTICALLY, to every decimal, in every rig. This is not a harness
fault and not a degenerate lane: the truss's top chord IS the chord path — the yard computes it
once and both lanes read it — and its web is structure hanging below, which carries no line. Two
conventions that differ enormously in material and not at all in where the line goes is exactly
the finding, and the two lanes sit at opposite ends of the rank so a viewer can put the near copy
against the far one.

(3) PEAK AND MEAN DISAGREE, which is the whole justification for the `scored` rung. At `level`,
chord, festoon and truss all peak at 0.6009 m — the festoon touches the datum's low point at a
bay boundary — so a worst-case score says the three are equally wrong. Their means are 0.4057,
0.3055 and 0.4057. One summary of the same thirteen numbers ranks them 1=1=1 and the other ranks
festoon 25% better.

THE FESTOON DIVERGES FROM THE FAMILY DELIBERATELY. All three member scripts build festoon as
their catenary at a bigger depth factor (1.15/0.45, 0.85/0.35, gravity_sag*1.2) — the same
construction at about 2.4x the amount, which is size wearing a name. The word names a REPETITION,
so this yard cuts each span into four bays and hangs the same solve in each. A catenary's sag
scales linearly with span at fixed slack, so the garland is exactly a quarter as deep as the
single curve (0.1502 against 0.6009 at level). Scaled instead of repeated it would have been a
deeper catenary with no independent reading at all; repeated, it has the same PEAK as the chord
and a mean a quarter smaller, which is a reading no other lane produces.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NOT RETYPED. slack_yard.gd opens with
const SLACK_SRC := preload("res://algorithms/wavefunctions/big_pipe_system/big_pipe_system.gd")
and every lane name comes out of SLACK_SRC.SLACKS at build time — the lanes, their order and
their count are the family's array, not a copy of it. _check_family_list() runs at _ready and
push_errors in both directions: a value the family declares that this yard has no builder for,
and a builder this yard has that the family has dropped. big_pipe_system is the one read because
nine of the twelve registry names resolve to its scene.

THE THREE ORDERS ARE ONE CONVENTION, and this was checked rather than assumed. All three scripts
in the family carry the BYTE-IDENTICAL const ["chord", "spline", "catenary", "festoon", "truss"]
(big_pipe_system.gd:82, cable_builder.gd:50, interactive_line.gd:43). What differs is the @export
default — big_pipe_system "spline", cable_builder "catenary", interactive_line "chord" — and each
member's registry list is that same const with its OWN default hoisted to the front. Predicted
against declared for all twelve tokens: three orders out of three, exact. So the registry order is
DERIVED from the code and has not drifted from it; there is no third vocabulary and no
disagreement about the word.

WHAT THE ORDERING ACTUALLY COSTS, which is narrower than it looks. build_dna_gallery trims a value
list from the TAIL, so three orders could mean three different values dropped first. In this family
they do not: all three orders end ...festoon, truss, so at caps 5, 4 and 3 every member is measured
on the SAME SET and only the tile order differs. Divergence appears only at cap 2 or 1, where
cable_builder would be measured on {catenary, chord} while the other eleven are measured on
{chord, spline}. The hazard is real and it has a threshold: a single-axis `slack` sweep at --max 3
or above compares like with like.

THE ORDER THIS YARD TOOK. It does not sweep `slack` at all (see dna.declines), so it takes no order
for that word. For its own two axes it reproduces the family's convention exactly — default first,
then the code's own declaration order minus the default:
  rig    code order level, bight, stepped, raked; default level, already first -> unchanged
  datum  code order none, beside, gauged, scored (the ladder, bottom up); default gauged
         -> gauged | none | beside | scored
At the gallery's DEFAULT cap of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2: rig keeps all four values and
datum is trimmed to [gauged, none], which is the ladder's two ends and the most informative
two-value truncation available. THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=16.
declines: `slack` AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS. Refused for the reason retention_corridor refused `retention`, and stated here so nobody reopens it: every one of the twelve members uses the word to stand in ONE convention and forgo the other four, so an axis over it would have five values each of which demolishes four fifths of this exhibit. The five values sit SIDE BY SIDE, not nested — spline does not contain chord, catenary does not contain spline, truss is not a deeper festoon — which is precisely the condition under which showing them all at once is NOT merely the top value, and is therefore the condition under which the retention_corridor move is available. The yard takes it: it stands all five and varies the PROBLEM. The word is exhibited, lettered on a tab at the head of each lane, and read out of the family's own const rather than retyped.

`filled` AS THE TOP RUNG OF `datum` — designed, built in the replica, measured, and cut. It filled the region between each run and the datum so the eye could read AREA rather than the worst gap. The argument was good and the geometry was fatal: five solid sheets standing in five parallel planes ranked in depth occlude each other from any oblique standpoint. A Python rasteriser of this exact geometry at the sweep's exact camera measured how much of each lane survives. At `filled` in the first layout: festoon 7.4%, spline 13.5%, catenary 23.2%, chord 62.1%, truss 100%. After the span was rotated onto Z and the pitch opened to 0.50 it was still only 40.2% at the worst, and raising the pitch to 0.60 bought 14 more points for 0.30 m of footprint. A rung that erases three of the five lanes it exists to compare is not a rung. `scored` replaced it, keeps the same argument (peak and mean rank the conventions differently) and cannot occlude anything, because it is three small marks standing outside the span. Measured at `scored` the worst lane is 72.4%.

PADDING THE CLOSEST PAIR. `gauged` vs `scored` is predicted at 5.45-7.05% focus depending on the rig, which straddles the critic's 6% twin bar, and it was left there. It is thin because `raked` and `stepped` are the rigs where the conventions are nearly right — spline's mean departure is 0.0373 m against 0.6793 at bight — so its score column is genuinely short and there is genuinely little to add. This is the field_room ruling: if a value is thin because the thing it describes is thin, say so with numbers and leave it. What WAS done is not padding but LAW 4: the columns were widened ACROSS the lanes, from 11 screen pixels to 27, because the critic resizes its crop to 160x160 before diffing and an 11 px mark in a 581 px crop is three samples — sorting_hall's three-pixel gauge exactly. Widening across the lanes buys screen width at 0.8138 per metre instead of 0.5810 and costs no span room.

A FRAME-RELATIVE GAUGE. Every mark is 1:1 in metres with no ceiling: a stick is the departure, a column is the mean departure, a collar is the peak departure, all measured from the kerb top and all directly comparable between lanes AND between rigs. A 0.1673 m column in the stepped frame and a 0.9800 m column in the bight frame are the same gauge reading different numbers. sorting_hall normalised each frame to its own busiest row and its gauge then said nothing about the quantity it existed to show.

A PROXY FOR THE DEPARTURE. The gauge measures the vertical distance from the run to the true curve at the station and nothing else. All five treatments are single-valued in the span coordinate — a catenary is a function of it, and so are a chord, a batten, a garland and a top chord — so the vertical is well defined for all five and no case can silently report zero. For `truss` the departure is taken on the TOP CHORD, the member that carries the line, not on the lowest point of its web; taking the web would have reported the truss as the worst convention by a factor of two and the number would have been about a girder's depth.

ANY ANIMATION, RATE, DURATION OR DECAY. A hanging line has obvious time-domain axes — a settling sag, a swinging span, a load ramp — and every one of them is invisible to a still PNG. info_board shipped five duration exports and produced six identical tiles. There is no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween and no physics body anywhere in this file.

RESCALING cable_builder's 0.45 m DRAWN DEPTH to this yard. It is 0.45 m here because it is 0.45 m there. The whole argument of the `spline` lane is that a drawn curve's depth owes nothing to the span it is drawn across; scaling the constant to fit would have retracted the claim while looking like tidiness, and it is the reason `bight` is a legible rig at all — 3.30 m of line across a 1.50 m gap falls 1.3605 m while the batten still draws its 0.45.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels,
because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic
crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background,
converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5%. The numbers
below come from rasterising this exact geometry at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62,
pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.55) in Python and pushing the result through that same
pipeline, with a painter's order that is exact for lane-against-lane occlusion because the lanes
are parallel planes at distinct depths.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS datum `gauged` <-> `scored`. That is the strong half of the claim and it rules
out the other twenty-one pairs: the three thinnest pairs in the whole sweep are this one rung at
three different rigs — raked 5.45%, level 6.68%, stepped 7.05% focus — and the fourth thinnest is
`none` <-> `beside` at raked, at 11.21%. Axis means over the 24 same-axis pairs each: datum frame
1.28% / focus 16.46% -> BITES; rig frame 5.54% / focus 45.84%.

WHICH RIG IT LANDS ON IS THE WEAK HALF, and it is stated as a dead heat rather than pretended to
be a result. `gauged` -> `scored` adds exactly three marks per lane and nothing else: a column of
height = mean departure, a stem, and a collar at the peak. Measured added change as a fraction of
the pair's own crop box:

  rig      sum of means  sum of peaks   added px   of crop   focus
  bight        3.3785 m      4.9928 m     24,887     9.07%   18.14%
  level        1.2219 m      1.9537 m     11,673     4.21%    6.68%
  raked        0.9680 m      1.5626 m      9,922     3.52%    5.45%
  stepped      0.7953 m      1.5707 m      9,156     3.51%    3.51% of crop -> 7.05%

`raked` and `stepped` cover 3.52% and 3.51% of their crops — the same number to two decimals — so
the ranking between them is decided entirely by grey-level contrast, which is exactly the part of
a flat-shaded replica least likely to survive Godot's showcase key light. The prediction is
therefore: 5-7% focus, on `gauged` <-> `scored`, at `raked` OR `stepped`. If it comes out at
`stepped` the prediction is not wrong, it is resolved.

WHAT DRIVES IT is that `scored` adds height proportional to the departures, and at the three quiet
rigs there is little departure to draw. At `raked` the columns are 27.0 px wide by 53, 6, 0, 40 and
53 px tall, with the spline and catenary columns effectively absent; at `bight` the same five are
155, 107, 0, 117 and 155 px. 3.3785 / 0.9680 = 3.49x the column height, and 24,887 / 9,922 = 2.51x
the pixels. Everything else in each pair of frames is identical to the byte.

IT WILL PROBABLY BE FLAGGED, AND THAT IS PART OF THE PREDICTION. 5.45% is under the critic's
TWIN_FOCUS bar of 6%, so the pair will be re-measured per channel — and per channel the same pair
reads 41.47%, because the columns are the sticks' orange (0.860, 0.340, 0.110) and the collars are
the datum's blue (0.360, 0.720, 0.850) against a neutral apron. It should land in the critic's
COLOUR-ONLY list, not in its twins list. If it lands in twins instead, the cause is that the
emissive materials washed toward white under the showcase key light, not that the rung is empty.

AND ONE PAIR THAT IS PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks like it should be.
`stepped` and `raked` have the SAME chord (3.1048 m) and therefore the SAME slack ratio (1.0629),
so they are the obvious candidate for a `rig` twin — the same amount of line over the same
distance. They are not twins and should measure far apart, because the ratio is the only thing
they share: stepped takes the rise in two steps and hangs two 1.65 m spans with a mast in the
middle, raked takes it in one and hangs a single 3.30 m span whose vertex sits at u = -0.590. Their
mean departures invert (spline 0.3346 at stepped against 0.0373 at raked; chord 0.1673 against
0.3380). If that pair DOES come back as the tightest `rig` pair, the slack ratio is doing more work
in the picture than the anchor layout, which would be a real finding and the opposite of this one.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS.
(a) If the closest pair comes back as `beside` <-> `gauged` instead, the replica understated how
    much the thirteen sticks smear under the 160 x 160 downsample. That pair measures 7.91% here
    and it is the one a hand estimate picks, because on the FULL-RESOLUTION tile it is the
    smallest pixel change of any datum pair (5,817 px against 5,070 for beside <-> scored). The
    two metrics genuinely disagree about this pair and the downsample is the reason.
(b) If `rig` comes back below about 20% focus, the replica's flat shading is the cause: it renders
    hard-edged untextured colour, so every rig pair saturates between 41.4% and 47.7% and the rig
    figure above should be read as "very large" rather than as a number.
(c) If any datum pair reads 0.00%, run tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=slack_yard first —
    a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL SIXTEEN FRAMES, not from the default. Union
2.30 x 2.25 x 3.30 (x = across the five lanes, z = along the span); diagonal
sqrt(5.29 + 5.0625 + 10.89) = 4.60896, radius 2.30448. The rig is
dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 puts the camera
at 2.30448 / 0.305731 x 1.9 = 14.3215 m and shows an 8.7571 m frame around a 3.30 m object — PAD
1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well
below 1.0.

AT 0.55 the camera comes to 7.8768 m and the frame to 4.8164 m, which is 157.80 px per metre.
Rasterised at that setting the subject's bounding box spans 77.5% of frame width and 63.0% of
height with 58 px of clear margin on the tight side, and the subject covers 21.5% of the frame —
far above the ~6% dilution floor and above the blank-render check. 0.50 was measured too (85.4%
of width, 26.2% subject) and rejected: 22 px of margin is not enough slack for the showcase key
light's specular fringe, which the replica does not model.

WHY THE UNION AND NOT THE DEFAULT: `level`, `bight` and `stepped` all top out at 1.85 m (mast 1.80
plus half a 0.10 crosshead) while `raked` reaches 2.25. Framing off the default would have seated
the camera closer and pushed raked's high mast toward the edge in the one frame that needed it.
The apron is deliberately the full 3.30 x 2.30 at EVERY value of both axes, so the box does not
move between tiles for any other reason.

GAUGE CHECK AT 157.80 px/m, because foresight_range shipped 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane.
Run 0.064 m -> 10.1 px; datum 0.048 m -> 7.6 px; gauge stick 0.040 m -> 6.3 px; truss web 0.038 m
-> 6.0 px; mast post 0.09 m -> 14.2 px; kerb 0.05 m -> 7.9 px; MIN_DEP 0.004 m -> 0.63 px, which
is the point of that threshold. The score column and collar are gauged against the BENCH as well
as the frame: the critic downsamples its crop 3.6x, so a mark must clear about 22 screen pixels to
survive as more than three samples. Widening them across the lanes rather than along the span buys
screen width at |right . x| = 0.8138 per metre instead of |right . z| = 0.5810 — column
0.07 x 0.5810 + 0.16 x 0.8138 = 0.171 m = 27.0 px = 7.4 samples; collar
0.10 x 0.5810 + 0.24 x 0.8138 = 0.253 m = 40.0 px = 11 samples.

LANE OCCLUSION WAS PART OF THE FRAMING DECISION and is why the span runs along Z rather than X.
Measured lane visibility at `gauged` went from chord 67% / spline 41% / catenary 53% / festoon 53%
/ truss 100% to chord 88% / spline 73% / catenary 68% / festoon 71% / truss 100%, for 0.20 m of
extra apron and a 0.4% change in camera distance. The measured dimension — the vertical departure
— does not foreshorten in either layout, so nothing about the measurement was traded for the
arrangement.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The
file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no
Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is
ungated: it reads config metadata, validates the family list and builds the whole yard standalone,
so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THE CATENARY SOLVER IS DETERMINISTIC BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the one place this artifact could
have leaked non-determinism. _solve bisects the arc-length condition
2a sinh(h/2a) = sqrt(L^2 - v^2) for a FIXED 96 iterations with no tolerance, no early exit and no
convergence test, so it does the same float arithmetic in the same order every time. Two captures
of one value are two photographs of one object.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps
config_rig / config_datum metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks the ancestor chain for
before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against
_is_rig / _is_datum, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready
has already built once — the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value.

BOTH AXES ARE String ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the
string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read
correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `datum`, by construction: the apron, the five kerbs, the masts and
crossheads, and all five runs. Those are the control. Everything that changes between the four
datum tiles is measurement apparatus, which is the axis's whole subject.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `rig`: nothing except the apron and the kerbs. The masts move, all five
runs change shape, and every stick and column changes length. `rig` should be by far the larger of
the two numbers, and if it is not, the sweep did not actually set it.

TWO LANES THAT SHOULD MEASURE THE SAME, AND IT IS NOT A FAULT: `chord` and `truss` have identical
departures in every rig, to every decimal, because the truss's top chord is the chord path — read
from the same array, not recomputed. The lanes still LOOK different (one is a line, the other is a
line with a girder under it), so this shows up in the departure table rather than in the pixels.
Do not "fix" it. It is finding (2) in dna.note.

NO TEXT NAMES AN AXIS VALUE. There are five Label3D in the artifact and they letter the five
conventions — chord, spline, catenary, festoon, truss — which are present at every value of both
axes. Not one pixel of any tile is a rendered word naming its own variant. Billboard is disabled
on all five, which also keeps LabelFramer out: it treats billboard-enabled as the hanging signal
and would otherwise bolt a panel and a bezel behind each one, five slabs this yard did not ask for.
Label3D is not a MeshInstance3D and does not enter the capture AABB.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D (BoxMesh for the set and
the score gauge, SurfaceTool for every tube), there is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG and no
particle system, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check three things before the design.
(1) Was --max at least 16? At the gallery default of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2 and `datum`
    is measured on [gauged, none] alone — which is the ladder's two ends, so the number would be
    large rather than faint, but it would be a verdict about two values published as a verdict
    about four.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 3.30 m yard is under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would
    be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? The five lanes rank in depth and the canonical camera sees
    them at 35.5 degrees off the span; a probe from directly above would separate them completely
    and one from along the span would stack them into one. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict
    on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.
